circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, has been the home of Formula One's season finale since 2009, designed by Hermann Tilke. It became the second Middle Eastern Grand Prix venue, following Bahrain and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a Melbourne street track encircling Albert Park Lake that annually hosts the Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside supporting racing series. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification for its motorsport facilities.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following extensive modifications and a name change, the track resumed hosting the Austrian Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street course in Azerbaijan's capital city positioned along the city's waterfront boulevard. At approximately 6 kilometres per lap, it ranks among the lengthiest circuits in Formula One's regular calendar. The venue has hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016 before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix and continues to feature the annual F1 race alongside various motorsport events. The track holds an FIA Grade 1 license and offers multiple layout configurations for different racing series and endurance competitions.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 km and features a versatile design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing all aspects of racing performance. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located in the Wallonia region of Belgium near the town of Spa, this 7-kilometre circuit has served as the home of the Belgian Grand Prix since 1925 and participated in Formula One's inaugural season in 1950. The track has maintained an uninterrupted presence on the F1 calendar since 1985, with only two absences in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary street circuit that hosts the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the venue has accommodated various international motorsport series including sports car racing championships and multiple North American racing categories.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in Jiading has been the primary home of China's Formula One race since its inaugural hosting in 2004, though the event was absent from 2020 to 2023 before returning to the calendar. Beyond Formula One competition, the venue began accommodating electric racing events in 2024, expanding its motorsport portfolio.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing venue positioned near Northamptonshire that serves as the permanent home of the British Grand Prix since 1987. The track gained historic significance by staging the inaugural World Championship race in 1950, and previously shared hosting duties with Aintree and Brands Hatch throughout the 1955-1986 period. Beyond Formula One, the circuit also accommodates MotoGP competition.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest became the first Formula One circuit in Eastern Europe when it hosted the Hungarian Grand Prix in 1986, remarkably completed in just eight months of construction. Located in Mogyoród outside the city, the 4. 381 km track was built after initial plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park were rejected by the Hungarian government in favor of a purpose-built facility.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Monza, located near Milan in northern Italy, is a 5. 793 km circuit established in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. The track hosts the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949, making it one of Formula One's most enduring fixtures, and earns its nickname "Temple of Speed" from its notably long straights and fast-flowing corner design.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, a 5. 807 km track in Mie Prefecture, Japan, is operated by Honda Mobilityland and hosts major international motorsport competitions. The venue, which accommodates 155,000 spectators, is particularly renowned for hosting Formula One and Japanese Super Formula championship races.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, running alongside the famous Las Vegas Boulevard where the city's premier resort casinos are located. The 3. 8-mile layout weaves past iconic venues such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, making it one of motorsport's most visually distinctive racing environments.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both accomplished drivers who died in racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue returned to hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix in 2015 after a 23-year absence, having previously featured the race on a different configuration until 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary track constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens featuring 3. 363 miles of racing surface with 19 corners, where qualifying speeds average approximately 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, the venue joined the championship calendar in 2022 and has since hosted the Miami Grand Prix as its primary event.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a compact 3. 337 km street course that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of Monaco, encircling the local harbour. Though formally named after the principality, it is widely known as the Monte Carlo circuit due to its predominant location within that neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km racing circuit that hosted the Dutch Grand Prix following its return to Formula One in 2021. The venue's partnership with the championship concluded after 2026.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is positioned near Lusail in northern Qatar, featuring a 5. 419-kilometer layout with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Brazil, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise racing circuit that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aircraft accident eight years earlier. The venue's facilities incorporate a dedicated kart track honoring fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah. It has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix annually since 2021 and began hosting a Formula E race in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a temporary road course that winds through Singapore's Marina Bay area, incorporating parts of the Downtown Core and Kallang districts into its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Montmeló, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced combination of extended straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple racing disciplines. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its facilities.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts major international motorsports events including MotoGP's Motorcycle Grand Prix of the Americas and endurance racing competitions, while previously accommodating various other series from NASCAR to IndyCar.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai and British racing driver who currently drives for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Fernando Alonso is a Spanish driver currently racing for Aston Martin in Formula One, bringing two world championship titles from his 2005-2006 tenure at Renault and 32 career Grand Prix victories across nearly two decades. Beyond single-seaters, he has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24-hour victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to capture both Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli joined Mercedes in 2025 and has already secured eight Grand Prix victories in his early Formula One career.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One for Audi, bringing his talent to the German manufacturer's team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing over a decade of experience to the grid. He finished second in the drivers' championship twice during his Mercedes tenure, and has secured ten race victories throughout his career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently competing in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan combines his European sports car racing commitments with a reserve role at Haas in Formula One, having participated in seven championship races during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly, a French Formula One driver, currently races for Alpine. He previously achieved a significant career milestone by securing victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while driving for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar is a Franco-Algerian driver competing in Formula One with Red Bull Racing under French nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently competing for Ferrari who has achieved seven world championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple performance records in the sport, including the most career race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One, bringing significant experience from his career in other motorsport categories. His achievements beyond single-seaters include victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while competing for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver currently races for Ferrari in Formula One, having secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning nine seasons. Leclerc finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while representing the Italian team.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: K-Mag is a Danish driver currently competing in endurance racing with BMW at WRT and part-time in NASCAR for Trackhouse Racing. He previously spent time in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014 to 2020 and again from 2022 to 2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently racing for McLaren, clinched the Formula One World Drivers' Championship in 2025 after securing 13 race victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French racing driver currently competing in Formula One for Haas. The former Alpine driver achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez is a Mexican driver currently racing for Cadillac in Formula One. The veteran competitor finished second in the 2023 championship while driving for Red Bull and has claimed six race victories throughout his lengthy career spanning 15 seasons.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver, races for McLaren in Formula One and has claimed nine Grand Prix victories during his time in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-year career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories over his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant competed in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously raced in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver currently racing in Formula One, where he competes for the Aston Martin team.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, transitioned to a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls after competing as a full-time Formula One participant throughout 2021-2025, taking on backup duties in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch and Belgian driver Max Verstappen races for Red Bull Racing under the Dutch flag, having secured four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12 seasons in Formula One, he has accumulated 73 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China as a racing driver currently holding a reserve role with Cadillac in Formula One. After competing in the championship across three seasons from 2022 to 2024, he holds the historic distinction of being the sole Chinese driver to have participated in Formula One competition.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Operating from its Enstone facility since 2021, this Formula One team has represented Renault's works effort under the Alpine brand name, following a rebranding from its previous Renault F1 Team identity. Backed by the French automotive manufacturer and the Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi Alliance, the squad maintained this works status until Renault's withdrawal from the sport at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has competed in Formula One through multiple organizational forms, with its current racing operation run by AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the motorsport arm of the Italian luxury automaker and stands as Formula One's most enduring and accomplished outfit, participating in every championship season from 1950 onwards. The squad, famously nicknamed after their iconic equine emblem, has established itself as the sport's most decorated competitor over its unbroken seven-decade tenure.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed F1 team founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas in 2014, the outfit commenced racing in 2016 with Ayao Komatsu assuming the principal role following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024 after leading the team since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss racing outfit established in 1970 by Peter Sauber, the company initially distinguished itself in endurance competition, notably winning Le Mans in 1989 alongside Mercedes-Benz. After joining Formula One in 1993, the independent constructor competed for over three decades before concluding operations in 2025, ranking fourth among the sport's longest-running teams by race entries before its acquisition by Audi AG to serve as the foundation for Audi's factory F1 programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One team headquartered in Woking that competes under corporate sponsorship. The organization operates as part of the McLaren Group and is owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 through both engine supply and team ownership, with the current operation based in Brackley under a German racing licence. Following a 2022 restructuring, the team operates as a three-way partnership between Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff. The marque's racing heritage carries the storied "Silver Arrows" identity.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as a second team within the Red Bull GmbH portfolio, alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with facilities near Milton Keynes, the squad operates as part of the Austrian conglomerate's dual-team strategy in the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced competition in 2024 as a sister team to Red Bull Racing under Red Bull GmbH ownership. Headquartered in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the team represents one of two constructor entities within the Red Bull motorsport portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, based in England under an Austrian licence, has been a dominant Formula One force since its 2005 formation by Red Bull GmbH. Christian Horner led the team throughout its two-decade history until 2025, when Laurent Mekies assumed the role as team principal. As one of Red Bull's two F1 entries alongside Racing Bulls, the squad has established itself as a major competitor in the sport.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's earlier unsuccessful racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team name.
